aboutH2: Into Action Recovery Sober Living: Men's Second-Stage House in East Vancouver
intro: Into Action Recovery Sober Living is a shared house for men in early recovery on East 12th Avenue in Vancouver, steps from Commercial Drive. It is where Into Action's residential graduates can live for a month or longer while they go back to work or school, under house rules and with other men doing the same.
It is housing with structure, not a treatment program. Treatment happens before, at Into Action's houses in Surrey, Burnaby and Abbotsford; this house is the step between that and living on your own.

pillars.title: A Shared Home Off Commercial Drive
pillars.body: The house is on a residential stretch of East 12th Avenue, a block from the cafes and shops of Commercial Drive and a short walk from the Commercial-Broadway SkyTrain station. That matters at this stage, because most residents are getting to jobs, classes and meetings across the city on their own. Into Action describes the home as modern, clean and safe, with shared bedrooms as the norm.

pillars.title: Freedom, With a Curfew
pillars.body: Residents have far more freedom than in residential treatment, but the house runs on rules. Everyone stays sober, takes random drug tests when asked, does a daily chore, keeps the curfew and goes to support meetings, at least four a week according to BC211. A counsellor visits weekly, and a house monitor who came through Into Action himself helps new residents find their feet.

pillars.title: Leaving When You Are Ready
pillars.body: There is no fixed end date. Into Action says the stay is typically 30 days and depends on each man's readiness, and BC211 says there is no maximum. Into Action frames this stage as practice for independent living: handling work, money and meetings while support is still in the house. It is optional, and men can also go straight home after First Stage.

overviewH2: Into Action Recovery Sober Living: Overview
overview: This house is for men who have stopped drinking or using and want a structured, sober place to live while they rebuild ordinary life. It is not the right fit for someone who is still using or needs treatment; for that, Into Action's residential houses come first.

location.heading: Into Action Recovery Sober Living in Vancouver, British Columbia
location.intro: The house is on East 12th Avenue in East Vancouver, just west of Commercial Drive and a few minutes' walk from Commercial-Broadway, where the Expo and Millennium SkyTrain lines meet. Downtown Vancouver is about 15 minutes away by SkyTrain or car, Burnaby around 15 minutes, Vancouver International Airport about 25 minutes, and Into Action's Surrey houses roughly 35 to 40 minutes.

faqIntro: Answers come from Into Action's own website, BC211 and public listings. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: Is Into Action Recovery Sober Living a treatment centre?
faqs.a: No. It is a sober living house, the Second Stage of Into Action's program. Residents have usually finished residential treatment already, and the house provides structure, house rules and peer support rather than a daily treatment program.

faqs.q: Who can live at the Vancouver sober living house?
faqs.a: Adult men in recovery. Most come from Into Action's First Stage residential program, and Into Action says most residents have over 100 days clean by this stage. BC211 notes the program also takes men with a strong support group and previous sober time, including men on methadone maintenance.

faqs.q: What are the rules at Into Action's sober living house?
faqs.a: Stay clean and sober, keep the curfew, do a daily chore and go to support meetings. BC211 lists a minimum of four support meetings a week and willingness to take random drug tests.
Usually 30 days or more. Into Action says the length depends on readiness, and BC211 says there is no maximum stay.

faqs.q: Can I work or go to school while living there?
faqs.a: Yes. That is what this stage is for. Many residents work, look for work or attend school while they keep up meetings, chores and the curfew.

faqs.q: Is there any counselling at the sober living house?
faqs.a: Some. Into Action's program page lists weekly on-site counselling and daily support meetings for Second Stage residents. There is no daily group therapy or medical care at the house.

faqs.q: How much does Into Action's sober living cost?
faqs.a: Into Action does not publish a price for sober living, and recovery.com has no pricing for it either. Call (604) 933-9003 to ask about cost and availability.
